newsitem.title: INDIA: Five militants killed in Kashmir clashes - police.
newsitem.headline: Five militants killed in Kashmir clashes - police.

text.p: Five separatist guerrillas were killed in two gun battles with Indian security forces in the Himalayan region of Kashmir, police said on Sunday.
A police official said three died in an eight-hour shootout on Saturday night at Niyedkhai village in the Baramulla district, 45 km (28 miles) north of Srinagar.
One army soldier was seriously wounded, police said.
In another clash between rebels and the Indian army in the nearby village of Sumbal on Saturday, two separatist guerrillas were killed, police said.
Two soldiers were wounded in the clash, which went on throughout the night, police said. A blaze destroyed two houses caught in the crossfire, they added.
Sumbal is 35 km (22 miles) north of Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir state, mainly Hindu India's only Moslem-majority region.
More than a dozen separatist militant groups are fighting for Kashmir's independence or for merger with neighbouring Pakistan.
India has repeatedly accused Pakistan of arming and training separatist guerrillas -- a charge Islamabad denies.
Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed in the state since the rebellion broke out in 1990.
